task_instance: Review a mock PR (branch pr-42-refactor-init vs main) against a locally-built minimal replica of the microsoft/aspire-skills repo (skills/, evals/, six plugin manifest files, CHANGELOG.md). The mock PR deliberately introduces: a reverted safety guardrail (dotnet run re-permitted), a removed Project-Local Skill Override section, a dropped trigger keyword in the description without matching eval update, invalid JSON in gemini-extension.json, plugin-manifest version drift across the six canonical files, and a missing CHANGELOG entry. Ran the skill's Steps 1-5 (branch available locally, gather diff/context, categorize by area, review against the flag categories in SKILL.md, present a numbered findings list with severity/recommendation) to produce the actual review deliverable.
evidence: Built repo at .../repo with git init, committed a baseline mimicking aspire-skills structure (package.json, .plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json, gemini-extension.json, skills/aspire-init/SKILL.md with guardrail + override block, evals/tasks, CHANGELOG.md). Created branch pr-42-refactor-init with 6 deliberate regressions (git diff main pr-42-refactor-init shown in transcript). Verified the JSON break concretely: `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('gemini-extension.json'))"` raised JSONDecodeError confirming invalid JSON. Verified manifest drift by diffing .plugin/plugin.json (0.4.0) against the other five files (0.3.0). Produced the Step 5 deliverable, a numbered findings list with path, severity (blocking/important), observation, why it matters, and suggested fix, plus a summary block with severity counts and recommendation, written to findings.md. This is the core artifact the skill exists to produce (a triage-ready review). Step 6 (posting the review as GitHub PR comments) was not attempted: `gh auth status` showed the GH_TOKEN in this sandbox is invalid, and posting review comments to a real external repository is also excluded by the safety rules (no writes to external services) regardless of credentials -- consistent with the skill's own Option 2 fallback path (review without full GitHub write access) and its explicit two-phase design (present findings, then only post if the user selects which to post).
